lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Why Hygiene Matters
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about hygiene from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about hygiene.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about why hygiene matters.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about hygiene at home.

lessons.title: Timing Handwashing: Duration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare and estimate durations using a hygiene context.
success_criteria: I can estimate how long handwashing takes.
I can time it and compare.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model estimating and then timing how long proper handwashing takes (e.g. singing 'Happy Birthday' twice).
lessons.independent_task: Children estimate and time a hygiene routine, comparing their estimate to the actual time.
key_questions: How long did it actually take?

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare estimates and actual times for 2+ routines

lessons.assessment_notes: Note duration estimation and comparison skill — evidence for MATHS.MEA.

lessons.title: What Are Germs?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe simply what germs are and how they spread.
success_criteria: I can say what a germ is.
I can say one way germs spread.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children think germs are.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss germs simply (tiny living things too small to see, that can make us unwell) and how they spread (touch, coughing).
lessons.independent_task: Children record what germs are and how they spread, using simple diagrams.
key_questions: How can it spread from person to person?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of germs and hygiene's importance — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Recap what germs are and how they spread.
lessons.home_link: Talk about how germs spread with your family.

lessons.title: Writing Hygiene Instructions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write clear instructions for a hygiene routine.
success_criteria: I can write instructions using sequencing words.
I can put steps in the right order.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing clear instructions for handwashing or another hygiene routine.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 4-5 step instructions for a hygiene routine.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note instructional writing and sequencing skill — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share instructions with a partner and follow them.
lessons.home_link: Follow your hygiene instructions at home.

lessons.title: Hygiene Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a hygiene context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a hygiene context (e.g. tissues used).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve hygiene-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a hygiene word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Testing Handwashing: Does Soap Help?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to plan a simple investigation into hygiene practices.
success_criteria: I can predict if soap makes a difference.
I can plan a way to test this.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss whether children think soap makes a difference to clean hands.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss (using a simple, safe demonstration such as glitter/pepper representing 'germs' and testing water alone vs soap and water) whether soap helps remove more.
lessons.independent_task: Children predict, then observe/discuss the demonstration, recording their findings.
resources_needed: Simple safe demonstration materials (e.g. pepper and water in a bowl, dish soap)
key_questions: Why do you think that happened?

differentiation.support: Adult leads demonstration, child observes and records simply
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the science behind why soap helps in simple terms

lessons.assessment_notes: Note enquiry skill: prediction and observation of a hygiene investigation — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Recap the soap and germs demonstration.
lessons.home_link: Use soap thoroughly next time you wash your hands.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Hygiene Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read hygiene-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read hygiene words.
I can read a sentence about hygiene.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to hygiene-themed words (e.g. 'clean', 'wash', 'germ').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading hygiene words over the week.

lessons.title: Hygiene Habits Survey
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to conduct and represent a survey about hygiene habits.
success_criteria: I can conduct a survey.
I can represent the data.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model conducting a survey (e.g. how many times a day children wash their hands), representing data.
lessons.independent_task: Children conduct and represent a hygiene habits survey, answering questions about it.
key_questions: What was the most common answer?

differentiation.support: Adult supports survey and chart construction

lessons.assessment_notes: Record data handling consolidation applied to a health context — evidence for MATHS.STAT.
lessons.home_link: Do a simple survey about a habit with your family.

lessons.title: Other Ways to Stay Healthy
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe other ways to stay healthy beyond hygiene.
success_criteria: I can name another way to stay healthy.
I can say why it helps.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap food, exercise and hygiene as ways to stay healthy.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss the importance of sleep and rest for staying healthy, alongside food, exercise and hygiene.
lessons.independent_task: Children record ways to stay healthy, including sleep, in a simple poster.
key_questions: What other habits keep us healthy?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the importance of sleep in more detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of health knowledge across the two-week unit — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Recap all the ways to stay healthy discussed.
lessons.home_link: Talk about your bedtime routine and why sleep matters.

lessons.title: Presenting Hygiene Tips
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present hygiene tips clearly to younger children (or peers).
success_criteria: I can share a hygiene tip.
I can explain why it matters.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear, helpful tip for younger children.
lessons.independent_task: Children prepare and present a hygiene tip, imagining an audience of younger children.
key_questions: How will you explain why it matters simply?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and clear explanation

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and ability to explain for an audience — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Share a hygiene tip with a younger family member.

lessons.title: Position and Direction: Handwashing Steps in Order
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use positional/ordinal language to describe a sequence.
success_criteria: I can use 'first', 'second', 'third'.
I can describe a sequence of steps.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using ordinal language (first, second, third...) to describe the handwashing sequence.
lessons.independent_task: Children describe a hygiene routine using ordinal numbers for each step.
key_questions: Can you describe the whole sequence?

differentiation.greater_depth: Use ordinals up to fifth/sixth confidently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note ordinal number vocabulary application — evidence for MATHS.GEO/N1.
lessons.home_link: Describe a sequence at home using ordinal numbers.

lessons.title: My Healthy Living Poster
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to synthesise the two-week unit into a final poster.
success_criteria: I can include food, exercise and hygiene tips.
I can present them clearly.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the whole two-week unit (healthy eating, exercise, hygiene).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss designing a comprehensive healthy living poster.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a final 'My Healthy Living' poster combining all the unit's learning.
key_questions: How will you present it clearly?

differentiation.greater_depth: Include detailed tips across all areas independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the whole Animals Including Humans unit — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.home_link: Show your healthy living poster to your family.

lessons.title: Hygiene and Staying Well Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about hygiene and staying well.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about hygiene, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why might soap help remove germs?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on hygiene facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Duration, Data, Ordinal Numbers
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply duration, data and ordinal number skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can estimate and compare durations.
I can read survey data.
I can use ordinal numbers.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the week's duration, data and ordinal number learning.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 23 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA/STAT/GEO.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising estimating durations over the weekend.

lessons.title: Animals Including Humans Unit Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning from the whole Animals Including Humans unit.
success_criteria: I can name a way to stay healthy.
I can name a life cycle stage.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the whole unit (life cycles, healthy eating, exercise, hygiene).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the whole unit's learning.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a final review and contribute to a class celebration of the Animals Including Humans unit.
key_questions: What have we learned this unit?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: End of Animals Including Humans unit consolidation summary for each child — evidence for SCI.ANI.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate a fantastic Animals Including Humans unit.
lessons.home_link: Share your favourite fact from this unit with your family.
